headline: Trainer-written checkpoints do not reload: a run at loss 0.4119 comes back at 36.12.
how_found: Building review item 6 (recovery checkpoints) and PROVING the resume rather than reasoning about it. Four 4-step CPT runs on the same recipe, GPU 1, CUDA 13.3.

C_recovered_from_A_step2.note: resumed at step 2/4, rng restored: python, torch_cpu, torch_cuda, numpy

D_warm_restart_from_A_step2.note: NO recovery involved — identical first loss to C, which isolates the fault

E_warm_restart_from_A_FINAL.note: the final checkpoint of a run that had just reached 0.4119

defect_1.what: save_checkpoint writes embeddings under wrapper-internal names the loader cannot reconstruct.
defect_1.evidence: quant_keys.json records method=int8_rowwise with 276 keys, but the file holds 279 scales. The three unrecorded ones are lm_head._emb, model.embed_tokens, model.embed_tokens_per_layer — written as lm_head._emb.weight / .embed_scale / .weight_scale, wrapper-internal names with no embedding_keys entry. load_causal_ckpt_quartet sets is_v2 = (method == int8_rowwise_v2 or embedding_keys present) = False, so it neither reconstructs the int8 embeddings nor matches those names, and the embeddings are effectively not loaded.
defect_1.impact: Every continuation is silently corrupt: booster runs, SFT initialised from a CPT checkpoint, anneal continuation, and crash resume all start from a model whose embeddings are garbage. The EVAL path is unaffected — it loads the same files correctly — which is why this survived: install numbers looked right while continuation was broken.
defect_1.not_caused_by: recovery.py. Arm D uses no recovery at all and reproduces the first loss exactly.

defect_2.what: The trainer still writes the v1/bf16 format; the v2 purge fixed artifacts but not the producer.
defect_2.evidence: A trainer-written checkpoint carries BF16 scales and BF16 embeddings ([262144,1536] and [262144,8960]) — ~5.5GB of bf16 storage. The artifact gate was run against one, symlinked into checkpoints/cpt: EXIT 1, wide={'BF16': 547}, e.g. lm_head._emb.weight.
defect_2.impact: The next real training run re-introduces exactly the bf16 storage the purge removed, and check_artifact_precision.sh goes red.

recovery_status: recovery.py itself is landed and works: arm C resumed at the right step with all four RNG streams restored, optimizer moments reloaded, and the continuation fingerprint accepted. End-to-end determinism CANNOT be demonstrated until defect 1 is fixed, because the weights the resume loads are already wrong before recovery runs. Item 6 is NOT complete.
bugs_in_my_own_code_found_by_running_it: The resume guard compared the FULL run fingerprint, which includes data.init_from — a value every legitimate resume must change. It refused the exact case it exists to permit. Fixed with continuation_fingerprint (same recipe minus init_from).
recovery.load used map_location=<training device>, handing set_rng_state a CUDA tensor: 'RNG state must be a torch.ByteTensor', minutes into the resume. Now always CPU, with a regression test.
